questions.stem: The Harappan site famous for the 'Great Bath' is:
questions.explanation: The Great Bath — a large public watertight tank (~12 m × 7 m × 2.4 m deep) with bituminous lining — is a centrepiece of Mohenjo-daro's citadel. Other signature structures — the Great Granary, College building. Harappa — two citadels, cemetery, granary. Lothal (Gujarat) — dockyard. Dholavira (Gujarat) — sophisticated water-management system + 10-sign signboard. UNESCO WHS for Dholavira (2021) and Rakhigarhi (large site in Haryana, still being excavated).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The only known Harappan dockyard was discovered at:
questions.explanation: Lothal — Gujarat — excavated by S. R. Rao. The rectangular brick-lined dockyard (~220 m × 37 m) connected to the Sabarmati estuary is the earliest-known in the world (~2400 BCE). Other Gujarat sites — Dholavira (urban planning, signboard), Rangpur, Surkotada. Kalibangan (Rajasthan) — ploughed field, fire altars. Banawali (Haryana) — 'mother goddess' terracotta. Chanhudaro (Sindh) — bead factory.

questions.stem: Harappan seals are most often made of:
questions.explanation: Most Harappan seals are of steatite (soapstone) — a soft stone that was carved, then hardened by firing. Square or rectangular, with an animal (unicorn, bull, elephant, rhinoceros, tiger) + short undeciphered script above. The famous 'Pashupati' seal from Mohenjo-daro shows a seated figure surrounded by animals. Seals were probably used by traders / officials as marks of identity or authority.

questions.stem: Match the Harappan site with the state (or region) where it lies. A. Rakhigarhi. B. Dholavira. C. Kalibangan. D. Banawali. List-II: 1. Haryana, 2. Gujarat, 3. Rajasthan, 4. Haryana.
questions.explanation: Rakhigarhi — Hisar district, Haryana (one of the largest Harappan sites). Dholavira — Rann of Kachchh, Gujarat (UNESCO WHS 2021). Kalibangan — Sri Ganganagar district, Rajasthan, on the banks of the dried-up Ghaggar. Banawali — Fatehabad district, Haryana. Most major Indian Harappan sites fall in Gujarat, Haryana, Rajasthan, Punjab.

questions.stem: The Harappan civilisation is notable for the lack of evidence of which of the following?

options.option_text: Large-scale temple structures or royal palaces

questions.explanation: Harappan sites have no identifiable large temples, royal burials, or monumental palaces — a striking contrast with contemporaneous Mesopotamia and Egypt. This makes the political / religious structure hard to reconstruct. They DID have — standardised brick sizes, cubical chert weights (binary/decimal ratios), grid-planned streets, covered drains, trade with Mesopotamia (via Oman / Dilmun), dockyards (Lothal).

questions.stem: The bronze figurine known as the 'Dancing Girl' was discovered at:
questions.explanation: The 10.5-cm bronze 'Dancing Girl' statuette (c. 2500 BCE) was found at Mohenjo-daro in 1926 by D. R. Sahni and is one of the earliest-known lost-wax bronze castings in India. On display at the National Museum, Delhi. Another famous Mohenjo-daro artefact — the 'Priest-King' steatite statue (now in Karachi). Harappa produced the red-sandstone 'dancing torso'.

questions.stem: The usual time range of the 'Mature Harappan' phase is:
questions.explanation: Harappan chronology — Early Harappan c. 3300-2600 BCE, Mature (urban) Harappan c. 2600-1900 BCE (the great city phase), Late Harappan / de-urbanisation c. 1900-1300 BCE. Possible causes of decline — climate change (weakening monsoon), drying of the Saraswati / Ghaggar-Hakra, shifts in trade, floods, or some combination; invasion theory is now generally discounted.
